hypothesis: The logic in AbstractCommandLineRunner.createDefineReplacements is too restrictive in how it parses the --define flag, failing to handle string literals correctly. Additionally, the RemoveConstantExpressions pass has an overly aggressive or incorrect logic for identifying and removing constant expressions.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the parsing logic in createDefineReplacements to correctly handle quoted strings (both single and double) and refining the logic in RemoveConstantExpressions to correctly identify which expressions are truly constant and safe to remove.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to the RuntimeException in createDefineReplacements when a flag like FOO="x'" is provided. The failure in RemoveConstantExpressions indicates that the logic for identifying constant expressions is incorrectly flagging non-constant or non-removable expressions.
reasoning_summary: The defect is primarily an algorithmic issue in how the compiler parses command-line flags and identifies constant expressions. It is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), but rather a flaw in the procedural logic used to process these inputs.
evidence_gaps: The exact implementation of the fix in RemoveConstantExpressions is not visible, but the failure pattern is consistent with an algorithmic error.
